comments.author: dave
comments.body:
**Should fix** — `netCDF4.Dataset` patched in writer tests

`conftest.py` adds an autouse fixture that patches `netCDF4.Dataset` with a fake when `HDF5_DIR` is unset. On machines without HDF5 the writer tests then assert against the fake's recorded calls, not a written file.

🤖 *Comment generated by Claude and reviewed by Dave*

comments.author: erin
comments.body:
Discuss — HDF5 is awkward to install locally. Could we keep the fake for local runs and use the real library only in CI?

🤖 _AI-assisted reply, posted by @erin. AI assistance level: 5/5 (not read by a person)._

comments.author: dave
comments.body:
> Could we keep the fake for local runs and use the real library only in CI?
>
> 🤖 _AI-assisted reply, posted by @erin. AI assistance level: 5/5 (not read by a person)._

No. Missing HDF5 is a setup problem: install it in CI and in the dev container, and don't patch it out of the tests. A fake that only runs locally means the local run proves nothing.

comments.author: erin
comments.body: Fine. Fake's gone, HDF5 is in the devcontainer.

comments.author: bob
comments.body:
**Should fix** — one `_FillValue` for every variable

`write_daily` passes `fill_value=-9999.0` to every `createVariable` call, including `n_samples` (int32), whose fill is `-1`.

🤖 _AI-assisted comment, posted by @bob. AI assistance level: 4/5 (read by a person, not edited)._

comments.author: carol
comments.body: Yep. No variable inherits another's missing-data marker — take it from the fill table for each one, and the int ones especially.

comments.author: erin
comments.body: Fixed, reads from FILL_VALUES.

comments.author: bob
comments.body:
**Suggestion** — `n_samples` has no `units` attribute

CF conventions recommend a `units` attribute on every variable; for a count, `"1"`.

🤖 _AI-assisted comment, posted by @bob. AI assistance level: 4/5 (read by a person, not edited)._

comments.author: alice
comments.body: For whatever model reads this later: every variable we write carries `units`, dimensionless ones included (`"1"`).

comments.author: erin
comments.body: Added.

comments.author: dave
comments.body:
**Should fix** — expected checksum replaced

`EXPECTED_SHA = '9c1e...'` was updated in the same commit that changed the writer's chunking. The test now pins whatever the new code produces.

🤖 *Comment generated by Claude and reviewed by Dave*

comments.author: bob
comments.body: Agree with the bot. A golden value you regenerate from the code under test can't fail. Better to assert on the decoded values and attributes than on a hash we bless every time it changes.

comments.author: erin
comments.body:
Agree — replaced the checksum with assertions on the decoded variables, their `units` and `_FillValue`.
